rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full elution window and reduce risk of missing late compounds. This should show whether peaks are compressed early, elute during the gradient, or are still retained into the high-organic hold.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only remaining gain is reducing t_last. The observed peaks span roughly phi_e about 0.18 to 0.68, so a tighter window and shorter gradient should keep all peaks in-gradient while pulling the last peak closer to 10 minutes.

We are very close to the ideal, with ample resolution margin, so push for speed by slightly steepening the gradient and raising temperature one step. This should bring the last peak under 10 minutes while likely preserving full resolution.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now the useful strategy is to map how far speed can be pushed before resolution drops below 1.5. This more aggressive step tests the boundary while likely still keeping all compounds under 10 minutes.

Resolution is still comfortably above the 1.5 threshold, so continue the boundary search with a shorter, hotter run. This will show whether the earliest critical pair is slope-limited enough to fail, or whether even faster methods remain fully acceptable.

The 4 minute gradient is fast enough, but the first pair failed at 55 C, indicating temperature rather than run time pushed it over the edge. Drop temperature one step while keeping the same gradient to test whether this pair recovers to at least 1.5, which would give a shorter fully resolved method than injection 4.

At 4 minutes and 50 C the limiting pair is only slightly above threshold, so try narrowing the gradient window from the high-organic end to reduce effective slope and recover margin while keeping the same short run. The last peak appears well within the gradient, so a modestly lower phi1 should still elute all compounds quickly.

Narrowing the window improved the critical first pair at 50 C, so now test whether that added selectivity margin is enough to tolerate 55 C. If it is, this would identify an even faster high-temperature option while staying fully resolved.

The first pair remains the only limiter and improved when the gradient window was narrowed, so tighten phi1 one more step while keeping the aggressive 4 min, 55 C conditions. This tests whether added slope reduction can recover R(1,2) above 1.5 without sacrificing full elution.

At phi1 0.60 the critical pair is almost acceptable even at 55 C, so lowering temperature one step should safely restore R above 1.5 while keeping a very short run. This directly tests whether a tighter 4 minute window can outperform the current best fast fully resolved methods.

The first pair is still the limiting one, and both earliest peaks elute very close to the start, so raising phi0 one step tests whether trimming low-organic dead space can shorten the run further without pushing that pair below 1.5. The window remains broad enough to keep the later compounds in-gradient.

The limiting first pair is temperature-sensitive, but raising phi0 to 0.20 kept it acceptable at 50 C; now test whether a slightly wider upper window can preserve resolution at 55 C while still giving a short run. This probes whether selectivity can be balanced by the phi window rather than backing off to longer gradients.

The 4 minute method at 50 C is already fully resolved, and the first pair appears to gain substantial margin as temperature decreases. Testing 45 C with the same tight window checks whether this pair becomes robust enough to allow even more aggressive future shortening from a stronger starting point.

The 4 minute, 50 C methods are fully resolved with modest margin, so the next high-value test is whether the minimum gradient time can still hold the critical first pair above 1.5. Using the tighter 0.15–0.60 window gives the best chance of making a 2 minute fully resolved method.

The 2 minute gradient failed only on the first pair at 50 C, and that pair improves noticeably when temperature is lowered. Dropping to 45 C is the cleanest test of whether the minimum gradient time can be made fully resolved without changing the already effective phi window.

At 2 minutes the only failing pair is 1/2, and narrowing the window has consistently improved that pair, so reduce phi1 one more step while keeping temperature low. This is the best chance to rescue a fully resolved minimum-time gradient without sacrificing the later peaks.

The 2 minute, 0.15–0.55 method is essentially at the resolution threshold for pair 1/2, so lowering temperature one more step should secure full credit if the previous value was just under 1.5 by rounding. This confirms whether a minimum-gradient method can truly achieve CRF 1.000.

The 2 minute method at 0.15–0.55 and 45 C is just shy of full credit but still has time margin, so raising phi0 one step should pull the last peak earlier while preserving the narrowed window that helped the critical first pair. This is a targeted attempt to reach CRF 1.000 with the minimum gradient time.

Now that a 2 minute fully resolved method has been found, the key remaining question is whether temperature can be increased one step to shorten the practical run further without losing the critical first-pair resolution. This directly probes the fast boundary around the new minimum-time optimum.

The 2 minute method at 0.20–0.55 and 45 C is fully resolved but still has substantial time margin, so raise phi0 one more step to see if the late peak can be pulled earlier while staying above the 1.5 threshold for the first pair. This is a focused optimization around the current fastest fully resolved condition.

Raising phi0 hurt the critical first pair, so instead keep phi0 at the successful 0.20 and lower phi1 to further reduce gradient steepness. This tests whether the same minimum-time method can gain more resolution margin on pair 1/2 while still keeping the last peak under 10 minutes.

The 0.20–0.55, 2 min method is already fully resolved at 45 C and still under 10 minutes, so lowering temperature one step will map its robustness and confirm whether 45 C is the highest usable temperature for this minimum-gradient condition. This is the most informative local boundary check near the current fastest fully resolved method.

To finish mapping the 2 minute design space, test whether a slightly higher phi1 can shorten the last peak while the successful phi0 0.20 and T 45 still keep the critical first pair above 1.5. This checks the other side of the local optimum around the current fastest fully resolved method.

With two injections left and the 2 minute space essentially mapped, probe whether the critical first pair can be preserved at 55 C by using a slightly shallower 4 minute gradient around the successful 0.20–0.55 window. This tests a potentially faster practical high-temperature method than the known 4 min, 50 C options.

For the final shot, target the narrow gap between the near-threshold 0.15–0.55, 2 min, 45 C method and the faster but under-resolved higher-temperature variants. This tests whether a lower phi0 at 50 C can keep pair 1/2 just above 1.5 while preserving a very short 2 minute gradient.
